messages:
alice: quick heads-up — saw a steady KV cache memory growth on prod-runtimes for long-context workloads (>8k). Not a GC leak; kv pages keep accumulating and compaction isn't keeping up.
ben: ugh. which metrics spiked?
alice: kv_mem_bytes up ~18% over 48h, kv_active_pages +15%, kv_evictions also ticked up. p95 latency creeped +10ms.
ben: any recent deploys that touch cache keying or session handling?
alice: only notable change was kernel-selector v3 (tuned batch window) + the session stickiness rollout for a subset of tenants. might be interaction.
cathy: can you paste a quick snippet of the profiler output?
alice: sure — this is from the runtime kv profiler (sample):
```
kv_mem_bytes: 3.7Gi -> 4.4Gi (48h)
kv_active_pages: 21.8k -> 25.2k
kv_frag_ratio: 0.38
kv_evictions/s: 7.2 -> 9.1
prefix_hit_rate: 0.42 -> 0.37
```

alice: the frag_ratio is the thing that worries me — we're allocating lots of tiny page fragments.
dave: do we still include session_id in the cache key for prefixes? that would explode key-space for long-lived prefixes.
ben: iirc current key format is: `tenant|model|session_id|prefix_hash` — which makes prefixes session-scoped by default.
cathy: that's the root cause for sure in mixed-traffic. per-request session ids + small variant tokens -> many near-duplicate prefixes that can't coalesce.
dave: solution options: 1) canonicalize prefix keys to drop session_id for prefix caching and keep session_id only for full-response entries, or 2) two-tier cache: shared prefix cache + session-delta cache.
ealice: ran a quick A/B on staging with key canonicalization (dropped session_id for prefix entries). results over 24h:
```
A: current keying
prefix_hit_rate: 0.36
kv_evictions/day: 1740
kv_mem_bytes: 3.9Gi

B: canonicalized prefix keys
prefix_hit_rate: 0.54
kv_evictions/day: 1360
kv_mem_bytes: 3.3Gi
p95 latency: -11ms
```

alice: hitrate up, evictions down, memory footprint shrank. promising.
eva: nice! did you break any tests where session-level personalization expects exclusive cached prefix?
alice: we ran regression tests — a small fraction (~0.7%) of sessions had subtle differences because they relied on ephemeral per-session prefix tokens. we added an opt-out header `X-No-Prefix-Share: 1` for those clients.
ben: can we instead bucket session ids (e.g., 4-8 buckets) so some personalization is preserved but key-space reduces?
cathy: yes. bucket approach is middle-ground: `session_bucket = hash(session_id) % 8` then key includes `session_bucket`. reduces fragmentation but keeps some isolation.
dave: long-term, we should implement explicit prefix namespace: `cache_key = f"{tenant}|{model}|PREFIX|v2|{prefix_hash}"` and a separate session cache for `DELTA|{session_id}`. allows different TTLs and compaction policies.
ben: agree. also consider proactive background compaction: when `kv_frag_ratio > 0.35` spawn defragmenter that coalesces small pages and migrates live entries.
cathy: sketch of compactor config we tested: 
```
compactor:
  enabled: true
  frag_threshold: 0.35
  max_drain_rate: 100 pages/s
  eviction_hysteresis: 0.1
```

cathy: in staging this reduced frag_ratio from 0.39 -> 0.28 over a day without impacting tail latency.
eva: any correlation with kernel-selector change? you mentioned batch window earlier.
alice: interestingly, kernel-selector v3 increased average batch latency slightly which means prefixes stay in working set longer before eviction policy triggers compaction window. might increase page residency and thus fragmentation when combined with session-scoped keys.
dave: so root cause: key-space explosion (session-per-prefix) + slightly longer batch windows => longer residency + more allocation churn => fragmentation.
ben: action items:
- canonicalize prefix keys for shared prefix cache (alice)
- implement session_bucket option behind flag (ben)
- add compactor with frag_threshold and test in prod canaries (cathy)
- add metrics: kv_frag_ratio, kv_small_page_count, prefix_shared_hit_rate (infra)

alice: i'll open PR for canonicalized prefix key and add opt-out header. will roll canary to 5% first.
infra-bot: deploy start: runtime/kv-keying-canary -> canary-5pct by alice at 3467890300
ben: i'll prototype session_bucket config and perf test.
cathy: i'll enable compactor on canary cluster and monitor frag_ratio.
eva: we'll monitor for the ~0.7% special cases; if they spike we'll revert.
dave: let's keep an eye on p99 latency while compaction runs.
alice: thanks folks — this may explain several long-context memory regressions we've had. good to have a plan. :thumbsup:
